root_cause: The WPC surface bulletin parser passes each coordinate token directly into _decode_coords, which assumes the token is already numeric apart from an optional leading minus sign. Archived CODSUS bulletins sometimes contain stray punctuation or uppercase letters embedded in otherwise valid coordinate tokens, so the decoder can build strings such as malformed lat/lon floats and raise ValueError instead of recovering the usable digits.
approach: After preserving the optional leading minus sign, strip non-digit characters from the remaining coordinate token before calculating the latitude/longitude split. Add a compact regression case to the existing WPC text parser test that includes punctuation and letter contamination in front coordinates. Keep the parser behavior otherwise unchanged, including the existing handling of unrecognized feature labels.
tests_to_add: Extend WPC surface bulletin parser regression to parse COLD/WARM front coordinates containing embedded quote and letter characters without raising ValueError.
risk_notes: Blindly removing non-digits could turn a severely malformed token into a plausible but wrong coordinate if the remaining digits are not actually intended as lat/lon.
out_of_scope_observations: Malformed feature labels such as TRmOF are still ignored by the current feature-name matching logic; warning about skipped lines is a separate behavior change.
